title: Gate what gets written
lesson: An unreviewed guess can repeatedly steer later runs to skip tests. An application write gate rejects that guess, keeps it in the current thread, and accepts a correction from an approved source for future retrieval.
transcript: 0–5.6s: Run 1 puts retry x3 in Thread 1, reads lint: strict @r12 from durable memory and shows an illustrative OK. The display then switches to Run 2 and a new empty Thread 2; this does not imply that saved checkpoints were deleted.
5.6–10.2s: Run 2 writes flaky: ci to its thread, then writes the unsourced tests: skip ? directly into durable memory. The record remains when Run 3 starts.
10.2–19.8s: Runs 3, 4 and 5 retrieve skip ? and show NO TESTS. Three red dots mark these illustrative skipped-test outcomes, not a claim of deterministic agent behaviour or failing test execution.
20.3–23.6s: A write gate and approved TESTS.md r13 source appear. The agent’s unsourced guess stops above the gate, bounces back and is kept in Thread 6.
24.1–27s: A green tests: run @r13 record travels from the approved source to the gate, passes, and replaces the old memory row. SAVED marks the completed write; it does not report an executed test.
27–32.2s: Run 7 and Thread 7 appear. The new run retrieves run @r13, then shows RUN TESTS. The result is held before the complete image fades to black.
limitations: Illustrative application logic: source/revision metadata alone does not prove approval or enforce permissions. The displayed source is assumed to have been reviewed.
Three repeated skipped-test outcomes illustrate risk, not a model capability or guaranteed failure rate. No actual agent integration or tests were executed.
The animation switches between threads. Older thread checkpoints may persist; deletion and retention are not demonstrated.
The gate blocks future writes; the already stored bad entry remains until the explicit replacement at 25.45s.
Audio was checked by decoded peak levels, scheduled-cue window energy and spectrogram, not listened to. Comparative evidence is in reviews/comparisons/memory-architecture/.
corrections: 21.6–24.7s: move packet entry, exit and rejection marks away from gate labels.
20.3–25.45s: show approved TESTS.md r13 as the correction source, then pass its record through the write gate.
11.6/15.3/18.5s: replace ambiguous FAIL badges with NO TESTS; 25.9s says SAVED and 29s says RUN TESTS.
Label each new thread separately; enlarge small record and gate text and widen thread rows.
